$comment: KNOWN divergences between the brand contract (.tastemaker/style-lock.md) and
the shipped pack (packages/css-engine/src/packs.ts), FEL-435.
Why this file exists. The two artefacts disagree on 7 values. Each is
internally consistent, and until now NO gate compared them — check_contrast.py
audits the lock, and nothing at all audits the palette that actually ships.
That is how `accent`/`border` came to be reported at 3.62 (+0.62 over the
3.0 floor) while the shipped pairing is 3.12 (+0.12). The number was right
about the contract and wrong about the product.
These entries are DEBT, not settled policy. Which artefact wins is a brand
decision escalated to Shane; a builder resolving it by editing one side would
be deciding it by fiat. Until that ruling lands, the divergences are recorded
with a reason and PRINTED on every run so they cannot go quiet.
check_palette_parity.py fails when:
- a divergence exists that is NOT listed here          (new drift)
- an entry here NO LONGER diverges                     (stale — reconcile and delete it)
So the gate is green today and loud on change in either direction. It is
deliberately not left permanently red: a gate that can never pass gets
disabled, which is worse than either artefact winning.
NOT LISTED, deliberately: `--graphite`. It has no counterpart in packs.ts.
`--color-neutral` is a separate token that style-lock.md:70 defines in its own
right, and packs.ts matches THAT line exactly. Pairing graphite (a brand ink)
against color-neutral (a component fill, with a near-white -foreground) was a
mapping error, not a divergence. It looked verified because the two coincide
in LIGHT (#363c47) and differ only in DARK.

divergences.reason: Near-identical warm off-white; unresolved which is canonical.
One-step difference in the dark paper value.
Lock raises surface to pure white above paper; the pack keeps surface equal to paper. A real design difference, not a typo.
The pack's dark accent is lighter/warmer than the lock's.
HIGHEST IMPACT. accent/border is 3.62 against the lock and 3.12 against the pack, over a 3.0 ui-safe floor. The shipped pairing has ~1/5 the headroom the tool reports.
Dark border, pack is slightly lighter/bluer.
Dark muted text, pack is slightly darker.
